text:
The dominant event of the period remains the KDP–JDE Peet's transaction. Keurig Dr Pepper's all-cash offer (EUR 31.85/share, EUR 15.7bn) proceeded through its full lifecycle within this dataset: the definitive agreement, the offer memorandum submission to the Dutch AFM, the unconditional declaration at 96.22% acceptance ("KDP Declares JDE Peet's Offer Unconditional"), settlement on 1 April 2026, and the post-closing acceptance period bringing KDP's stake to 97.75% ("KDP Acquisition of JDE Peet's – Post-Closing Acceptance Period Results"), with statutory buyout proceedings now underway for the remainder. Corporate-structure follow-through includes JDE Peet's delisting from Euronext Amsterdam (30 April 2026), conversion to a private B.V., a post-closing demerger, and consent solicitations to restructure EUR 3.35bn in outstanding Euro Notes across six series. KDP's board appointment of Aaron Alt and the naming of Rafael Oliveira as CEO of the planned Global Coffee Co. confirm the reaffirmed 2027 separation plan, with JDE Peet's positioned as its core.

On regulation, EU packaging rules are now binding: the Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation (PPWR) entered into force on 12 August 2026, directly naming JDE Peet's brands (Jacobs, L'OR, Senseo, Tassimo, Douwe Egberts, Kenco, Pickwick, Moccona) as in scope for design-for-recycling, PFAS restrictions, and Extended Producer Responsibility obligations, with the Declaration of Conformity deadline following on the same date and the Commission's updated FAQ signaling a supportive rather than punitive initial enforcement posture. In parallel, the EU Deforestation Regulation (EUDR) compliance deadline of 30 December 2026 is approaching, with the Commission issuing a corrigendum clarifying how coffee roasters and decaffeinators fit within due-diligence obligations and separately extending EUDR coverage to soluble coffee — both relevant to JDE Peet's instant coffee lines. This suggests JDE Peet's compliance workstreams will need to cover both packaging and sourcing traceability simultaneously in the coming months.

On the competitive and consumer front, reporting on premium beverage pricing at Starbucks and Blank Street ("Coffee shop pricing strategies") is characterized as analysis rather than confirmed fact, but suggests continued normalization of higher price points across the category, a dynamic consistent with JDE Peet's own reported reliance on pricing (19.5% in FY2025, per its full-year results) over volume growth.

On supply chain, coffee futures remained volatile: Colombian port disruptions at Buenaventura contributed to a sharp price drop in mid-August, while ICE Arabica futures separately fell to a three-week low in late July. The EU's formal signing of the International Coffee Agreement is a notable policy development for trade and pricing stability, though its practical implications for JDE Peet's are not yet detailed in the available data.
